entries.why_wrong: `len` is a builtin that's always available — Python never requires an import for it, so that's not what's throwing here. The actual failure is that `len(items)` is one past the last valid index, so indexing with it raises an IndexError.

Direct element access on a list is 0-based too, just like slicing — there's no separate rule that makes `items[k]` fail while slices work. The real problem is the value used: `len(items)` sits one past the last valid index (0 to n-1), so the lookup raises an IndexError.

Naming a parameter `items` doesn't shadow anything Python treats specially, and shadowing a name isn't what triggers a runtime error here anyway. The crash comes from indexing with `len(items)`, which is one past the last valid index for the list.
